Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat Ibrahim (Sura of Abraham)

It is Meccan, except for the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Have you not considered those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude﴾ up to His words: ﴿And indeed, your return is to the Fire﴾. And Allah knows best.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra﴾. Its meaning: "I am Allah, the All-Seeing." It was also said its meaning is: "I am Allah, the Most Gracious."

And His words: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you﴾ mean: this is a Book which We have sent down to you.

And His words: ﴿to bring mankind out of darknesses into the light﴾ mean: from misguidance to guidance, from disbelief to faith, and from error to right direction. It was also said: from innovation to the Sunnah.

Darkness (ẓulmah) is the blackening of the atmosphere in a way that prevents sight, and light (nūr) is a radiant whiteness by which sight is achieved. His words: ﴿by the permission of their Lord﴾ mean: by the command of their Lord. It was also said: by the knowledge of their Lord.

And His words ﴿to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾: the path (ṣirāt) is the religion, and the Mighty, the Praiseworthy is Allah the Exalted. The meaning of "Mighty" (ʿazīz) is the Dominant, and the meaning of "Praiseworthy" (ḥamīd) is the One who deserves praise in His actions, because He is either bestowing favour or acting justly.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 2:

And His saying: ﴿Allah, the One to whom﴾ is recited with both the nominative (raf') and the genitive (khafd). Whoever recites it in the genitive, it is an attributive continuation (masbuq) of His saying: ﴿the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. And whoever recites it in the nominative, then it is by way of the estimation (taqdir): "He is Allah."

And His saying: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ means: to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And His saying: ﴿And woe to the disbelievers﴾. Al-wayl (woe): it is a valley in Hell. It was also said that it is a supplication for destruction. ﴿from a severe punishment﴾ means: a great punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 3:

His saying: ﴿Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter﴾ means: those who give preference to the life of this world over the Hereafter. The meaning of preference (al-iythar) is seeking the world without regard for the Hereafter, by taking from wherever one finds it, and not caring whether it is forbidden (haram) or permissible (halal). It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "A time will come upon people when a man will not care whether he takes wealth through what is lawful or through what is unlawful."

His saying: ﴿and who bar [others] from the way of Allah﴾ means: they refrain from accepting the religion of Allah, and they prevent people from accepting it. His saying: ﴿and seek to make it crooked﴾ — crookedness (al-awaj) applies to religion, and also to a spear or a wall. The meaning of the verse is: they seek the religion of Allah to be deviant. It was said: they seek the way of Allah while deviating from the right course. It was also said: they seek ruin for Muhammad. It is said that the pronoun refers to the world, and the meaning is: they seek the world by way of deviation from the truth, and that is through the means of what is forbidden, as we have stated.

His saying: ﴿those are in far-off error﴾ means: in extended error.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people﴾. The wisdom in this is that when He sends a messenger with the language of his people, they understand his speech and comprehend from him. If someone says: God, exalted is He, sent the Prophet to all creation, as he said: "I have been sent to the red and the black" (al-ahmar wa'l-aswad), and He did not send him with the language of all creation?

The answer to this: all of creation follows the Arabs in the call, and he was sent with their language. Then he sent messengers to the regions, calling them to God, and he translated his speech for them.

His saying: ﴿that he may make [it] clear for them﴾ its meaning is what we have explained. His saying: ﴿so God leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ its meaning is apparent.

His saying: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ we have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 14, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We had already sent Moses with Our signs, [saying]: "Bring your people out of darknesses into the light"﴾, meaning: from disbelief (kufr) to faith (iman).

And His saying: ﴿And remind them of the Days of Allah﴾. It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he said: its meaning is: the blessings of Allah. In some musnads this has been transmitted as a marfu' report traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). The second view: "the Days of Allah" means the vengeances of Allah. Some of them said: the events of Allah, meaning: what He inflicted upon the past nations. It is said: "So-and-so is knowledgeable about the Days of the Arabs," meaning: about their battles (waqa'i').

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for every patient, grateful one﴾. As-Sabbar (the patient one) is one who is greatly patient, and sabr (patience) is restraining the self from what the self inclines towards. It has been narrated from ash-Sha'bi that he said: "Patience is half of faith, and gratitude is half of it, and certainty is faith entirely." As-Shakur is one who is greatly grateful.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 6:

And the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And [remember] when Moses said to his people, "Remember the favor of Allah upon you"﴾ – the verse – meaning: the bounty (minnah) of Allah upon you.

His saying: ﴿When He saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who inflicted upon you the worst torment﴾ – we have already explained this in Surah al-Baqarah.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and slaughtered your sons﴾ – He said in one place without the waw (wa, "and"), and here He said it with the waw. Mentioning the waw implies that the slaughter was preceded by another torment, while omitting the waw implies that the torment is the slaughter itself.

And His saying: ﴿and spared your women﴾ – meaning: they would leave the women unkilled. In a report: "Kill the elderly of the polytheists, and spare their young (shaykh-hum, sharkhahum)." ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾ – it has been said that the trial (bala') is a test (mihnah), and it has been said that the trial is a blessing (ni'mah), and the place of the blessing lies in the deliverance from the trial. It has also been said that its meaning is: a great test from Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 7:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed﴾, meaning: your Lord made known (a'lam), and ta'dhin (proclamation) is ilam (making known), and adhin and mu'adhdhin (the one who proclaims) is the one who makes known. The poet said:

(And you did not perceive the light of dawn until we heard the adhin in our mosques)

And His saying: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾. Shukr (gratitude) is acknowledging the blessing with a sense of humility toward the Benefactor. It is related that Dawud (peace be upon him) said: "O Lord, how can I thank You, when I cannot fulfil Your thanks except through a new blessing from You?" He said: "O Dawud, now you have thanked Me."

It is also narrated that a man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Advise me, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Hold fast to gratitude, for it is an increase."

The meaning of the verse: If you give thanks to Me through monotheism (tawhid), I will surely increase you in the blessing of the Hereafter over the blessing of this world. It was also said: If you give thanks through obedience, I will surely increase you in reward.

And His saying: ﴿But if you are ungrateful﴾, meaning: deny (judahtum). ﴿Indeed, My punishment is severe﴾, meaning: great (la-'azim).

Almost none of this passage needs adjustment beyond translation, but I'll render it in full.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Moses said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth all together, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.﴾ That is: Free of need from His creation, Praiseworthy in His actions.

Tafsir al-Quran of al-Sam'ani on surah 14, verse 9:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Has there not come to you the report of those before you?﴾ That is: the news of those before you.

(﴿...after them, none knows them except Allah. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands to their mouths and said, "Indeed we are...﴾ the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, and those after them, none knows them except Allah.) It is narrated from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he recited this verse and then said: "The genealogists have lied." Some of them transmitted this as a report traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ). And from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "Between Ibrahim and ʿAdnan, the grandfather of the Messenger, there are thirty generations, none knows them except Allah." And from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: "What lies beyond ʿAdnan back to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, none knows except Allah." And from Malik ibn Anas that he disliked a person tracing his lineage father by father back to Adam, and likewise in regard to the Messenger he disliked it, because no one knows those forefathers except Allah.

His saying: ﴿their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾ means: with manifest evidences. His saying: ﴿but they put their hands to their mouths﴾ is narrated from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, who said: "They bit their hands in rage." The poet said:

(Were Salma to see the wasting of my body, a thread upon the bone of my leg and my hand,
and after my family and the harshness of my kin, she would bite the tips of her hand out of longing.)

And another said:

(His rage has consumed his fingertips, so he remains biting upon his hoof.)

The second opinion regarding the verse: when the prophets said, "We are messengers of Allah," the disbelievers placed their hands upon their mouths, meaning "Be silent." This was transmitted by al-Kalbi and others.

The third opinion: the meaning of the verse is that they denied the messengers in their statements. It is said: "I rejected so-and-so's saying in his mouth" when one calls him a liar.

The fourth opinion: the "hands" here are blessings, and the meaning is: they rejected what, had they accepted it, would have been bounties and favors.

His saying: ﴿in their mouths﴾ means: with their mouths, that is: with their tongues, in denial. The most correct of these sayings (ashraq al-aqawil) is the first, and the third is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas.

His saying: ﴿and they said, "Indeed we have disbelieved in that with which you have been sent"﴾ means: we have repudiated what you were sent with.

His saying: ﴿and indeed we are in doubt concerning that to which you invite us, [a doubt] unsettling﴾ means: troubling (murib). Doubt (shakk) is wavering between two opposite positions.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Their messengers said: "Is there doubt about Allah?"﴾ Its meaning: there is no doubt about Allah. This is an interrogative in the sense of negating what they believed. And His saying: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ means the Creator of the heavens and the earth. And His saying: ﴿He invites you so that He may forgive you of your sins﴾ Abu 'Ubayda said: "min" (from) is redundant (ṣila), and its meaning is: so that He may forgive you your sins.

And His saying: ﴿and defer you to a specified term﴾ means until the time of the completion of your lifespans. And His saying: ﴿They said: "You are only human beings like us. You wish to turn us away﴾ i.e., to prevent us ﴿from what our fathers used to worship.﴾ The meaning is clear. And His saying: ﴿So bring us a clear authority﴾ i.e., a clear proof [and miracle]. And "sultan" (authority) here is the evidence that brings the one who opposes back to the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 11:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Their messengers said to them, "We are only humans like you"﴾, meaning: we are nothing but humans like you. ﴿But Allah confers His favor upon whom He wills of His servants﴾, meaning: He bestows favor upon whom He wills of His servants with prophethood. It has also been said: with success (tawfiq) and guidance.

And His saying: ﴿It was not for us to bring you an authority except by the permission of Allah﴾, meaning: with a proof and a miracle. ﴿Except by the permission of Allah﴾, meaning: by the command of Allah. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, the meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And what is [the matter] with us that we should not rely upon Allah?﴾ Its meaning: "And what reason do we have not to rely upon Allah? For we know that nothing is attained through effort except after Allah, exalted is He, has decreed and destined it."

His saying: ﴿And He has already guided us to our ways.﴾ That is: He has guided us to the paths of truth.

His saying: ﴿And we will surely bear with patience whatever harm you inflict upon us.﴾ The verse is an instruction to the believers and a guidance to them to be patient in the face of the harm of those who oppose the truth.

His saying: ﴿And upon Allah let those who rely [upon Him] rely.﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 13:

And His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely expel you from our land, or you will return to our religion."﴾ We have already explained this in Surah al-A'raf, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿or you will return to our religion﴾.

And His saying: ﴿So their Lord inspired to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers."﴾ That is: the polytheists (al-mushrikin).

And His saying: ﴿And We will surely settle you in the land after them﴾ means: We will make their dwellings the place of your residence. This is in the sense of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves﴾.

And His saying: ﴿That is for whoever fears My standing (maqam)﴾. The difference between al-maqam and al-muqam: al-maqam is the place of standing/residence, while al-muqam is the act of standing/residing. If it is said: how can there be a maqam for God, when He has said: ﴿That is for whoever fears My standing (maqam)﴾? We say: the people of tafsir have unanimously agreed (ajma'a ahl al-tafsir) that its meaning is: that is for whoever fears His standing before him, and this is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens﴾.

And His saying: ﴿and fears My threat (wa'id)﴾, i.e., My punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 14, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they sought victory﴾. Its meaning: they sought help (istansarū). In a report: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek victory (yastaftiḥ) through the poor emigrants (ṣaʿālīk al-Muhājirīn)," that is, he sought help from God by means of their right.

And His saying: ﴿And every obstinate tyrant was disappointed﴾. "Disappointed" (khāba) means: lost. It was also said: "destroyed" is every tyrant. The jabbār is the one who sees no one above him. Al-jabarīyah is the seeking of elevation with no limit beyond it, and it is a description that is proper only to God; as for its use in describing creatures, it is blameworthy. It was also said: al-Jabbār is the one who compels creation to his will. As for al-ʿanīd, it is the one who opposes the truth.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Hell is before him﴾. Most of the scholars say its meaning is: Hell is in front of him. A poet said:

(And behind you is a day you will reach, / neither a present one who can escape it nor one who goes out [of it].)

That is, in front of you. And Abu ʿUbayda said:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 16:

His saying: ﴿And before him is Hell﴾ means: after him is Hell. And his saying: ﴿And he will be given to drink of purulent water﴾ means: of water which is purulence (ṣadīd). Ṣadīd is what flows from the disbelievers of pus and blood, and the origin of ṣadīd is the water that comes out of a wound mixed with blood and pus. It has also been said: "of purulent water" means: of water like ṣadīd.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 17:

And His saying: ﴿yatajarra'uhu﴾ means: he drinks it sip by sip, from its bitterness and severity. And in a hadith, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When he brings it near his face, it scorches his face and the skin of his head falls off; and when he drinks it, his intestines are cut to pieces and come out from his anus."

And His saying: ﴿wa-la yakadu yusighuhu﴾ means: he does not swallow it. It was also said that its meaning is: he almost does not swallow it, and [if he does] he swallows it only so that it boils in his belly. And His saying: ﴿wa-ya'tihi al-mawtu min kulli makan﴾ — Ibrahim al-Taymi said: from every hair of his body. It was also said: death comes to him from in front of him and behind him, from above him and from beneath him, and from his right and from his left.

And His saying: ﴿wa-ma huwa bi-mayyit﴾ means: he suffers the severity of death, yet he does not die. This is in the sense of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿la yamutu fiha wa-la yahya﴾. And His saying: ﴿wa-min warai'hi 'adhabun ghalizun﴾ means: severe. The harsh punishment is abiding in the Fire.

The Exalted said: ﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes on which the wind blows violently﴾. The place of the likeness lies in His words ﴿like ashes on which the wind blows violently﴾, meaning: the violent wind carried it away.

As for His words ﴿on a stormy day﴾, there are two meanings.

The first: He described the day as stormy because it contains stormy wind, just as one says "a hot day" or "a cold day," meaning that heat or cold is in it. The poet said:

(Two cloudy days and a day of sun...)

The second meaning: ﴿on a stormy day﴾, that is, on a day of stormy wind. The poet said:

(And the mail-shirts' gleam laughs at our skins when a day of darkened sun comes, eclipsing [it])

That is, eclipsing the sun.

As for His words ﴿They have no power over anything of what they have earned﴾, this is because their deeds have gone and become void, like the ashes that the stormy wind carried away.

As for His words ﴿That is the far-off error﴾, it means the long-lasting straying.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 19:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Do you not see that Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth?﴾ The meaning of "He created the heavens and the earth with truth" is: that He set within them the proofs of His oneness and all His other attributes.

And His words: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you﴾ mean: if He wills, He can destroy you. ﴿And bring a new creation﴾ means: a different people, and this is in the sense of the words of the Most High: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people other than you﴾.

It has been said in the tafsir: "a people more obedient to Allah than you."

And His saying: ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah﴾ means: not hard (ʿazīz, "difficult, mighty"). That is because all things are easy and simple in terms of power, and nothing is difficult for Allah, however great or mighty it may be.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will come out before Allah all together﴾, meaning: they will come forth from their graves to Allah, all together.

And His saying: ﴿Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers"﴾. The meaning of "those who were arrogant" is: those who were haughty toward the people and haughty against faith, and they are the leaders and chieftains.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, we were your followers, so will you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?﴾ "We were your followers" means: we were your followers (atba', plural of tabi'). ﴿So will you avail us anything against the punishment of Allah?﴾ means: will you repel from us anything of the punishment of Allah? And His saying: ﴿They will say, "If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you"﴾: its meaning is, if Allah had guided us, we would have called you to guidance, but since He led us astray, we called you to misguidance.

And His saying: ﴿It is all the same for us whether we show anxiety or whether we are patient﴾. Concerning the reports, they say: "Some peoples in the world showed anxiety and were saved, so we will show anxiety that we may be saved." So they show anxiety for a long duration and see no deliverance. Then they say: "Some peoples in the world were patient and were saved, so we will be patient that we may be saved." So they are patient for a long duration and see no deliverance. After that they say: ﴿It is all the same for us whether we show anxiety or whether we are patient﴾.

His saying: ﴿We have no place of escape﴾ means: no refuge and no deliverance. It is said: they will show anxiety for a hundred years and be patient for a hundred years. It is also said: so-and-so fell into ḥays bays (a state of confusion and no way out), and ḥāṣa wa-bāṣa, when he fell into a matter from which there is no escape.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 22:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And Satan will say, when the matter has been decided﴾. His words: ﴿when the matter has been decided﴾, meaning: when the people of Paradise have entered Paradise and the people of the Fire have entered the Fire.

In some reports it is said: "A pulpit of fire will be placed for Iblis, and he will ascend it and address them," and that is when they cling to him and say: "You are the one who did this to us."

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke my promise to you﴾. The promise of truth is that which is certain to be fulfilled. His words: ﴿but I promised you and broke it to you﴾ refer to that which will not be fulfilled. It is also said that he will say to them: "I told you there is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Fire," and other such things.

His words: ﴿And I had no authority over you﴾, meaning: I did not bring you any proof for what I called you to. His words: ﴿except that I called you﴾ — this is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), and its meaning is: "but I called you," that is, I made it appealing to you. His words: ﴿so you responded to me﴾, meaning: you answered me. His words: ﴿So do not blame me, but blame yourselves﴾, meaning: do not turn your blame toward me; turn your blame toward yourselves.

His words: ﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me﴾, meaning: I cannot be your helper, nor can you be my helper. It is also said that the meaning is: I cannot save you, nor can you save me. Hamzah recited: "وَمَا أَنْتُم بِمُصْرِخِيَّ" with a kasra on the ya' (ي). The grammarians do not accept this reading, but al-Farra' cited a line of poetry that supports Hamzah's recitation. It is said that it is the dialect of the Banu Yarbu'. The poem:

(He said to her: "Are you, O seeker...?" She said to him: "You are not the one who is accepted.")

His words: ﴿Indeed, I disbelieved in what you associated with me before﴾. There are two opinions on this. The first: "I disbelieved in your making me a partner with Allah in worship and obedience." The second: "I disbelieved before you associated me with Him in worship," meaning: I disbelieved before your disbelief.

His words: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment﴾, meaning: painful, severe.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 14, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be admitted into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ — we have already explained it. ﴿Abiding therein﴾ — remaining in them forever. ﴿By the permission of their Lord﴾ — by the command of their Lord.

His saying: ﴿Their greeting therein will be, "Peace."﴾ Concerning the one who greets with peace, there are three opinions:

One of them: that the one who greets with peace is Allah, exalted is He. The second: they are the angels. The third: that the one who greets with peace is some of them upon others.

﴿Have you not seen how God presents a parable: a good word﴾. The *mathal* (parable) is a well-known saying used to liken one thing to another in meaning. As for His words ﴿a good word﴾, the commentators (*mufassirun*) agree that the good word here is: there is no god but God.

As for His words ﴿like a good tree﴾, most of the people of *tafsir* (Qur'anic exegesis) hold that the good tree here is the date palm. This has been clarified by the report of Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his Companions: "Tell me about a tree that is like the believer." The Companions thought of the trees of the desert. Ibn ʿUmar said: "It occurred to my mind that it was the date palm, but the Prophet said: 'It is the date palm.'" Ibn ʿUmar said: "I mentioned to my father that it had occurred to my mind, and he said: 'If you had said it, it would have been dearer to me than red camels (*ḥumr al-naʿam*).'"

In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "Honour the date palm, for it is your aunt."

Its meaning is that it was created from the excess of the clay of Adam.

The second view is that the good tree is a tree in Paradise. This has been related from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was also said that the good tree is the coconut tree (*jawz al-Hindi*).

As for His words ﴿its root is firm﴾, meaning: firmly fixed in the earth. And His words ﴿and its branches are in the sky﴾, meaning: its highest parts reach into the sky.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 25:

And His saying: ﴿It yields its fruit every season﴾. Al-hin (ḥīn) in the language means "time." Regarding the meaning of al-hin there are several opinions. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Six months, because it is from the time of its pollination (ḍirāb) until the time of its emerging (iṭlā')." Mujahid said: "Al-hin here is a full year, because the date palm bears fruit every year."

And from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, he said: "Four months, because it is from the time of its appearance (ẓuhūr) until the time of its ripening (idrāk)." Some others said: "Two months, because it is from the time it is eaten until the time it is harvested (yuṣram)."

The fifth opinion: that it is morning and evening, because the fruit of the date palm is always eaten from it, either as rutab (fresh dates), or as tamr (dates), or as busr (unripe dates).

And His saying: ﴿by the permission of its Lord﴾, meaning: by the command of its Lord. And His saying: ﴿And Allah sets forth parables for the people﴾. The point of the parable is that faith is firmly established in the heart, and the deed ascends to heaven, like the date palm whose root is firmly fixed in the earth and whose branches rise up to heaven. The point of the parable in His saying: ﴿It yields its fruit every season﴾ is that the benefit and blessing of faith never cease, but reach the believer at every time, just as the benefit and blessing of the date palm reach those who need it at every time.

Some of them argued that the date palm resembles the human being, because it needs pollination (liqāḥ), just as a human is not born to him until he is fertilized. His saying: ﴿So that they may remember﴾, meaning: that they may take heed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 26:

The Most High's saying: ﴿And the likeness of an evil word﴾: the evil word is shirk (associating partners with God). And His saying: ﴿like an evil tree﴾: they differed concerning it. Anas ibn Malik said: it is the colocynth (al-hanzalah). It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: it is garlic (al-thawm). And it has been said: it is the dodder (al-kashutha), which is al-'ishqah.

And His saying: ﴿uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability﴾: meaning, it is torn up from the surface of the earth. And His saying: ﴿having no stability﴾: meaning, it has no firmness. The real sense is that it has no firm root in the earth, nor a branch that rises up to the sky. The point of the parable is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 27:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah makes firm those who believe with the firm word﴾. The firm word (al-qawl al-thabit) is the word of Tawhid (monotheism), which is "There is no god but Allah." He said, ﴿Allah makes firm﴾, because He is the One who establishes faith in the hearts of the believers.

His saying: ﴿in the life of this world﴾ means: before death. His saying ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾ means: in the grave. This is the view of most of the exegetes (ahl al-tafsir). It has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) through the narration of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, and it is the saying of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, and a group of the Companions.

Know that the questioning in the grave is established in the Sunnah, and belief in it is obligatory, and numerous reports have come concerning it. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) was at a funeral, and he mentioned to his companions that two angels come to a man in his grave and question him, saying: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?" He said: "As for the believer, he says: 'My Lord is Allah, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your place had you said otherwise.' Then a door to the Garden is opened for him, and his grave is made spacious as far as the eye can see. As for the disbeliever, the two angels say to him: 'Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?' He says: 'I do not know.' They say: 'You did not know, nor were you guided.' Then a door to the Garden is opened for him, and they say: 'This was your place had you answered.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and his grave is constricted upon him until his ribs interlock, and they strike him with a hammer of fire, and he cries out a cry that every creature hears except the two jinn and humankind."

In some reports: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If anyone were to be saved from the punishment of the grave, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh would have been saved. Yet the grave squeezed him a squeeze or two squeezes." It is also reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to 'Umar: "How will you be when two angels come to you..." [the report continues]. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, and will my intellect be with me?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then I will suffice against them."

It has been said: the punishment of the grave has three parts: one third for those who neglect cleansing from urine, one third for backbiting, and one third for walking about with tale-bearing. And Allah knows best.

There is another view regarding the verse: that "the life of this world" is the grave, and "the Hereafter" is the Resurrection. The first view is more correct.

His saying: ﴿And Allah sends astray the wrongdoers﴾ means: He does not guide the polytheists to this answer, nor does He inspire them with it. His saying: ﴿and Allah does what He wills﴾ refers to granting success, abandonment, making firm, and not making firm.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude﴾ and so on. There are three opinions concerning it. The first: they are the disbelievers of Quraysh. The second: they are the leaders of the polytheists at Badr; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. The third: it is related from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was asked about this verse and said: "They are the two wicked clans, the Banu al-Mughirah and the Banu Umayyah. As for the Banu al-Mughirah, they were killed on the Day of Badr, and as for the Banu Umayyah, they were given enjoyment for a time."

And His saying: ﴿and caused their people to alight in the abode of perdition﴾, i.e., the abode of destruction, which is Hell. The poet said:

(Indeed Luqaym, and indeed Luqman, wherever they perished...)

meaning: they perished.
And His saying: ﴿Hell, which they will enter, and what an evil place to settle⁠—﴾ its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they set up rivals to God﴾, meaning: partners and equals. Hassan ibn Thabit said in verse:

(Do you satirize him, when you are not his equal? ... So your evil is for the good of your father, the ransom.)

Know that God has neither an opposite (didd) nor a peer (nidd). As for the peer (nidd), which is the like, it is well known. As for the opposite (didd), it is so because it contains a sense of likeness, and God has no like in any respect whatsoever.

His saying: ﴿That they may lead astray from His way﴾. Error is attributed to them only because they are the cause of (the going astray). This is like the speaker who says: "The world has tempted me," attributing the temptation to the world, because it is the cause of temptation. His saying: ﴿That they may lead astray from His way﴾, its meaning is apparent.

His saying: ﴿Say: Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: If a disbeliever were in the utmost misery and harm, not finding rest by night or by day, that would be a blessing in comparison with what he will come to in the Hereafter; and if a believer were in the most pleasant of livings, that would be misery in comparison with what he will come to in the Hereafter.

His saying: ﴿For your destination is the Fire﴾, meaning: your return is to the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 31:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say to My servants who have believed: Establish prayer⁠﴾ — this is a report in the sense of a command, meaning: establish the prayer (ṣalāh). And His saying: ﴿and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly⁠﴾ — meaning: openly and not openly. It is also said: voluntary spending in secret, and obligatory spending openly.

And His saying: ﴿before there comes a Day in which there is no trade (bay') nor any ransom⁠﴾ — Abu 'Ubayda said: meaning there is no ransom (fidā') therein. ﴿Nor any friendship (khilāl)⁠﴾ — meaning no companionship nor affection, and this is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous⁠﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 32:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down water from the sky, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

And His saying: ﴿And He subjected for you the ships to run upon the sea by His command﴾, meaning: by His knowledge and His permission.

And His saying: ﴿And He subjected for you the rivers﴾, meaning: He made the rivers submissive to you, so that you may channel them wherever you wish.

And His saying: ﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, constantly pursuing their courses﴾. That is for your benefit, and the subjection of the sun and the moon is their running in one uniform manner in what returns to the interests of the servants.

And His saying: ﴿constantly pursuing their courses (dA'ibayn)﴾, its meaning is that they neither slacken nor stop. Al-da'b (dA'b) in a thing is to proceed in one habitual manner.
And His saying: ﴿And He has subjected to you the night and the day﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 34:

And His saying: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾. It has been recited in two readings. The well-known reading is: ﴿min kulli ma sa'altumuhu﴾ (of all that you asked of Him), and it is also recited: "min kulli ma sa'altumuhu" with shaddah and tanwin. The well-known saying, its meaning is: that is, of all that you asked of Him.

If someone says: "We ask Him for things and He does not give us?" The answer: that its kind gives to humankind, even if He does not give each specific thing. Thus the statement is sound on this basis. It is also said that its meaning is: of all that you asked of Him and you did not ask of Him. As for the second reading, the meaning of "ma" is negation, and its meaning is: He gave you things you did not ask for, for indeed Allah the Exalted gave us the night, the day, the sun, the moon, the stars, the winds, and what is similar to that, and we did not ask Him for any of them.

And His saying: ﴿And if you count the favour of Allah, you will not enumerate it﴾. Abu al-Aliyah said: its meaning is: you cannot count them. It is also said: you cannot thank Him for them.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is a wrongdoer, a disbeliever﴾. It means: wrongdoing toward himself, disbelieving in his Lord. It is said: this verse was revealed specifically concerning Abu Jahl. It is also said: it was revealed concerning the kind of disbelievers in general. It is permissible to mention "al-insan" (mankind) and mean by it the kind of people, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾. It is also said: [the wrongdoer] is one who thanks other than the one who bestowed favour upon him, and the disbeliever is one who denies his benefactor.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 35:

His words: ﴿And when Abraham said: My Lord, make this city secure, and keep me and my sons far from worshipping idols﴾. They are unanimous that the city is Makkah. His words ﴿secure﴾ mean: possessing security.

His words ﴿and keep me and my sons far from worshipping idols﴾ mean: keep me and my sons distant from the worship of idols. If someone says: Abraham was protected (ma'sum) from worshipping idols, so how is his supplication for himself correct, when many of his offspring worshipped idols? Where is the answer?

The answer: As for Abraham, the supplication is for an increase in protection (al-'ismah, divine preservation from sin) and steadfastness. As for his sons, it is said: the supplication was for his sons from his loins, and none of them worshipped an idol. It is also said: his supplication was for those of his sons who were believers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 36:

And his saying: ﴿My Lord, they have indeed led many of the people astray﴾ attributes the misguidance to them (the idols), due to the meaning we have explained. And his saying: ﴿Whoever follows me, then he is of me﴾ means: he is of the people of my religion.

And his saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys me, then You are indeed Forgiving and Merciful﴾ may bear two interpretations:

The first: that he said this before Allah informed him that He does not forgive shirk (associating partners with Allah).

The second: that what is meant by disobedience here is what falls short of shirk.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 37:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled﴾ mean: I have caused to dwell. The words of the Exalted: ﴿some of my offspring﴾. The offspring (dhurriyyah) here is Isma'il, peace be upon him, and his mother Hajar.

In the narrative: he carried Hajar and Isma'il, who was a suckling infant, and all three were on the Buraq. He brought them to the place of the House, and it was a red mound of earth. Jibril said to him: "Here you have been commanded." So he set Isma'il and his mother down at the place of the Hijr, and he set off returning to Syria. Then Hajar called out to him: "O Khalil Allah (the Friend of God), to whom are you leaving us?" He said: "To Allah, the Exalted." She said: "We have accepted that." The story concerning this is well known.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿in a valley without cultivation﴾. He said this because Makkah lies between two mountains, and it is a valley.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿by Your Sacred House. Our Lord, that they may establish prayer﴾. He named it "sacred" (muharram) because what is forbidden there is not forbidden elsewhere.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So make hearts among the people incline toward them﴾. Afidah (hearts) is the plural of fu'ad (heart). Ibn 'Abbas said: "If he had said 'afidat al-nas' (the hearts of the people), it would have crowded you with [Persians] and Romans." In another narration: the Turks and the Daylam. In another narration from someone else: the Jews, the Christians and the Magians would have performed the pilgrimage.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿and incline toward them﴾ mean: yearn for them. Al-Suddi said its meaning is: "Make their hearts inclined toward this place, for a person inclines with his heart wherever it inclines."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿and provide them with fruits﴾. In some reports: Allah the Exalted uprooted a village from Syria with its trees and its land and placed it in the location of al-Ta'if. The words of the Exalted: ﴿that they may be grateful﴾ have an apparent meaning.
The Most High's saying: ﴿Our Lord, You surely know what we conceal and what we reveal, and nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven﴾. Its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 39:

And His saying: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq﴾. In the narrative: Isma'il was born to him when he was ninety-nine years old, and Ishaq was born to him thirteen years after that. It is also said: Isma'il was born to him after he had reached one hundred and [seven] years. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 40:

His saying: ﴿My Lord, make me one who establishes prayer, and [make] from my descendants [such]﴾ means: from among those who establish the prayer with its limits (ḥudūd) and its pillars (arkān), and who guard it. His saying: ﴿and from my descendants﴾ means: make from my descendants those who establish the prayer. His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and accept my supplication﴾ means: respond to my supplication.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 41:

His words: ﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr read: ﴿wa-liwalidayya﴾ (and my two parents), and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Yahya ibn Ya'mar read: "wa-liwalidati" (and my mother). The well-known reading is ﴿wa-liwalidayya﴾ [as given in the Qur'an as "wa-liwalidayya"].

If someone says: How could he (Ibrahim) seek forgiveness for his parents when they were not believers?

The answer to this: It has been said that his mother had embraced Islam. As for the father, he only sought forgiveness for him before it became clear to him that he persisted in polytheism, and we have explained this earlier. It has also been said: "my parents" refers to Adam and Eve. And it has been said: Nuh and the mother of Ibrahim.

In the Tafsir of al-Damyati: that His words ﴿and my parents﴾ mean ﴿and my child﴾. Ibn Faris said: this is permissible in the language, namely that the word "walid" (parent) is used in the sense of "mawlud" (offspring), as one says "ma' dafiq," meaning "madfuq" (gushing). And His words ﴿and for the believers﴾ are clear in meaning.

And His words ﴿on the day when the reckoning will be established﴾ mean: on the day when Allah calls the creation to account.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 42:

The words of His, the Exalted: ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do﴾ — to the end of the verse. Ghafla (heedlessness) is a state that prevents a person from grasping the reality of matters. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "This verse is a consolation and solace for the one who has been wronged, and a threat to the wrongdoer."

His words: ﴿He only delays them﴾ mean: He only gives them respite. His words: ﴿For a Day when the eyes will stare fixedly﴾ mean: out of dismay, bewilderment and the severity of the matter. The meaning of "tashkhas" (stare fixedly) is that they will be raised up and removed from their places.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 43:

And His saying ﴿Muhti'een﴾ (hurrying forward with outstretched necks). Most of the scholars hold that its meaning is "hastening" (musri'een). Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Tha'lab said: al-Ihta' (ihţā', the lowering of the gaze) is looking in (humiliation and submission). It was also said: muhti'een means "those who keep their gaze fixed, not blinking." The sense of hastening that we mentioned is that they do not turn right or left, do not know the places of their feet, and have no concern or attention for what they are being driven toward.

And His saying: ﴿Muqni'ee ru'usihim﴾ (raising their heads). It is said: aqna'a ra'sahu means he raised his head, and aqna'a ra'sahu also means he lowered it. If the intended meaning is raising, then its sense is that their eyes are directed toward the sky, looking to see what will come upon them from Allah the Exalted. If iqna' is understood as lowering the head, then its sense is: lowering their heads and bowing them down. The poet said:

(I bowed my head toward him and lowered it, as if he were seeking something he hoped to obtain.)

And al-Mu'arrij said: they raised their heads until they almost placed them upon their shoulders.

And His saying ﴿Their gaze will not return to them﴾, meaning: their gaze will not come back to them. It is as if the things before them have distracted them, so they look at nothing else.

And His saying: ﴿And their hearts are a void (hawa')﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: "torn apart, not taking in anything." Qatadah said: their hearts came out of their chests until they reached the throats, because of the intensity of that day and its terror. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And the hearts will reach the throats﴾. Accordingly, His saying ﴿and their hearts are hawa'﴾ means empty, and from this the air was named hawa' because of its emptiness. It was also said: empty of intellect, as though they had departed from fear and dread.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "And their hearts are hawa'" means wavering, not settling in one place. It was also said: hawa' means hollowed out by cowardice and terror. Hassan ibn Thabit said:

(Be informed, Abu Sufyan, from me, for you are a hollow, empty, hawa'.)

The true meaning of the verse is that the hearts are displaced from their places, and the eyes are fixed in staring because of the terror of that day.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 44:

And His saying: ﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them﴾ means: warn the people of fear (khawf).

His saying: ﴿Then those who did wrong will say, "Our Lord, grant us respite for a short term"﴾ means: give us a reprieve.

And His saying: ﴿for a short term﴾ is a request for a return (raj'ah), as if they were asking to be sent back to the world.

And His saying: ﴿We will answer Your call and follow the messengers﴾ its meaning is apparent. And His saying: ﴿Had you not previously sworn﴾ means: you swore in the world. And His saying: ﴿that there would be no decline for you﴾ means: there is no resurrection for you, no recompense, and no reckoning.

And His saying: ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves﴾ — meaning: they wronged themselves, so We destroyed them. And His saying: ﴿And it became clear to you how We dealt with them﴾ — meaning: you came to know Our punishment of them.

And His saying: ﴿And We set forth for you the parables﴾ — meaning: the likenesses (al-amthal, sing. mathal, "parables"), and its sense is: We made clear that your situation is like theirs.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 46:

The Almighty's words: ﴿And they have indeed plotted their plot﴾ mean: they devised their scheming.

And His words: ﴿Yet their plot is with Allah﴾ mean: with Allah is the recompense for their plot.

And His words: ﴿Though their plot was such that the mountains would thereby be moved﴾ are recited in two readings: "litazūla" and "litazīla." al-Kisa'i alone recited it with a fatha on the lam.

As for His words: ﴿litazūl﴾ (with a kasra on the lam, which is the reading of most reciters), its meaning is: "Their plot was not such that the mountains would thereby be moved," meaning that their plot does not remove the affair of Muhammad, which is firm like the firmness of the mountains.

It has also been said: the meaning of the verse is to show the weakness of their scheming and plotting, and that it does not reach this degree. As for His words: "And though their plot was such that the mountains would thereby be moved," with a fatha on the first lam and a damma on the second, the meaning is: even if their plot reached such magnitude against Muhammad that it could move the mountains, they would not be able to remove the affair of Muhammad. ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas and a group recited: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains were about to be moved from it." It is also reported from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he recited: "Had it not been for the word of Allah, the mountains would have been moved by their plotting."

It is related from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the meaning of the verse, that it was revealed concerning Nimrod when he said: "I will surely ascend to the heaven." He took vultures and fattened them, then made a chest (tabut), set wooden poles at its corners, and placed meat on their tops. Then he tied the feet of the vultures to the poles and released them, and the vultures rose up. Nimrod sat in the chest with his chamberlain, and it is said: with a boy of his. The chest had two doors: a door above and a door below. He said: "When the vultures rose into the sky and a day passed, he said to his boy: open the lower door." Then the earth appeared like a sea of water. He said: "Open the upper door," and the sky was as it was. Then another day passed, and he said: "Open the lower door," and it was opened, and the earth appeared like smoke. He said: "Open the upper door," and it was opened, and the sky was as it was. Then he ordered his boy to lower the heads of the vultures and the poles, so the chest came down to the side of the earth with a great crash. The mountains feared that a command had come from the sky and were nearly moved from their places. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And though their plot was such that the mountains would thereby be moved﴾ (with a fatha on the first lam and a damma on the second) ﴿from it, the mountains﴾.

There is another opinion regarding the verse, which is the saying of Qatadah: its meaning is: "And though their shirk was such that the mountains would thereby be moved," and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿The heavens are almost rent asunder from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains fall down in ruins, that they ascribe to the Most Merciful a son﴾.

The words of God, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not think that God will fail His messengers in His promise﴾. It is said that this is of the inverted type (maqlub), and its meaning is: "fails His messengers in His promise." His words: ﴿Indeed, God is Almighty, Owner of retribution﴾. We have already explained the meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 48:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will come forth [from their graves]﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: This earth will be changed into a white earth like silver, on which no blood has been shed and no sin has been committed. As for the heavens, they will be changed into heavens of gold.

The second view was stated by Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir and Muhammad ibn Ka'b: that the earth will be changed into an earth of bread from which people will eat. Abu Ja'far recited: ﴿And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾. The well-known view regarding the verse is that the changing of the earth is its alteration from one state to another, like a man saying to another: "You have changed after me" (tabaddaltu ba'di), meaning your appearance and condition have altered. The changing of the earth is by moving its mountains, levelling its rivers, flattening its valleys, uprooting its trees, and making it a level plain (qa'an safsafan) in which you see no crookedness or elevation. As for the changing of the heavens, it is by altering their condition: by folding up their sun and moon, the scattering of their stars, and their becoming at one time like red oil (ka'l-dihan), which is red leather, and at another time like molten brass (ka'l-muhl). It has also been said that the meaning of the change is that He will make the heavens into gardens and the earths into fires. This has been authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) through the narration of Masruq from ʿAʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, regarding His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth﴾, where will people be at that time?" He (ﷺ) said: "On the Sirat (bridge)." When this is established, then this view is the preferable one.

We were informed of this hadith by Abu ʿAli al-Hasan ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Shafiʿi, who said: Abu al-Husayn ibn Faris said: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' said: My grandfather Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Shaʿbi, from Masruq, from ʿAʾisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ)... the report.

As for His saying: ﴿And they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾, its meaning is: they will come out of their graves before Allah, the One, the Subduer, who will judge among them by what He wills.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 49:

His saying: ﴿And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in shackles﴾. It is said: "sofadahu" (he shackled him) when he bound him, and "asfadahu" (he gave him) when he gave him. Al-A'sha said:

(You were my guest one day, and he honored my seat, and gave me [a gift], as a leader, despite my infirmity.)

Here "asfadani" means: he gave me. His saying: ﴿bound together﴾ means: placed with one another in chains and fetters. It is also said: every disbeliever will be bound with a devil in every chain and fetter. This was reported by al-Kalbi. It is also said: his two legs will be drawn up to his neck and he will be fettered, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿bound together in shackles﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Their garments of pitch⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿—﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿—

Let me correct that and translate properly.

The passage is:

"And His saying: ﴿Their garments (sarabil) of tar (qitran)﴾, meaning: their shirts are of tar. Qitran is that with which camels are daubed (tahna'u bihi al-ibil) for scabies. Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ikrimah recited "min qitr'an", meaning: from molten brass (safr muadhdhab), (he said): whose heat has reached its limit. And it was said: from molten copper (nuhas muadhdhab) whose heat has reached its limit. The people of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: He only mentioned that their shirts are of tar because fire spreads to it most quickly in catching alight.

And His saying: ﴿And the Fire will cover their faces﴾, its meaning: the Fire will rise over their faces. It was said: will burn them (tusla)."

Wa qawluhu: ﴿Liyajziya Allahu kulla nafsin bima kasabat﴾ yaʿni: ma kasabat min khayrin wa sharr.

Translation:

Regarding His words, ﴿That God may recompense every soul for what it has earned﴾, He means: for what it has earned of good and evil.

And His words, ﴿Indeed God is swift at reckoning﴾, its meaning is: swift in recompense. The reality of ḥisāb (reckoning) is the enumeration of what a person has done, good or evil, so that he may be recompensed for it.

This is the commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 14, verse 52:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿This is a message (balagh) for mankind﴾ means: this Qur'an, and this which I have sent down to you is a message for mankind, that is, in it is a conveyance (tabligh) to mankind. His words: ﴿and that they may be warned thereby﴾ mean: that they may be frightened by it.

And His words: ﴿and that they may know that He is but one God﴾ mean: that they may derive evidence from these verses for the oneness (wahdaniyya) of God, exalted is He.

And His words: ﴿and that those of understanding may take heed﴾ mean: and that those of understanding (ulu al-albab), that is, those of intellect (ulu al-uqul), may be admonished. In some of the exegetical works it is reported that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. And Allah knows best.
